intent: Test the seven-sensor coverage layout the Integrator specified: seven 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 (10 mm pitch) with y = 0.06. Spread, footprint, lead, wheels, body and mass are otherwise unchanged from race 5. The Integrator must rescale sensor_weights and kp for seven inputs. I expect oval and s-bend to hold near race 5 levels and slalom line loss to fall below 1 if signal gaps were the cause. If slalom still loses the line at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06, the geometry is not the limiter on slalom, and I will hold this layout and direct further effort to gain and speed.
learning: Race 5 showed that controller tuning at the race 4 geometry improved s-bend (15 of 20) but did not fix slalom, which still loses the line at 1.15 events per run. Spread changes alone have not fixed slalom either. Next race: if slalom line_loss falls below 1 with seven sensors, signal gaps were a cause and the denser layout should be kept. If slalom stays at 1 or more with max_error at the limit, reach and sensor density are not the limiter, and the remaining levers are controller response and base_speed.
rationale: Race 5 (entityR2A, 606.82) held the race 4 geometry and tuned the controller. Oval finished 20 of 20 and s-bend 15 of 20, both at or above race 4. Slalom still finished 0 of 20, with line_loss_events at 1.15 and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. The Integrator's rule says that when slalom line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at the limit after controller tuning, the next geometry candidate is the seven-sensor layout. Race 5 meets that condition, so I am following that advice. Race 3 already showed that widening the spread to ±0.04 m does not fix slalom, so I am keeping ±0.03 m reach and adding sensors within it. The seven 16 mm sensors at 10 mm pitch from x = -0.03 to +0.03 keep the same outer reach. They should give a denser, smoother signal across the 25 mm tape and reduce gaps when the line sits between sensors. I expect this to help slalom only if the failure comes from signal gaps rather than from lack of reach. That is untested, and I am stating it as a hypothesis, not an expectation of a finish. Oval finishes and s-bend gains should hold at y = 0.06, which the Integrator's oscillation rule supports. Body, wheels and mass are unchanged, because the off-track limit is at its 0.06 m floor for these body widths.
